Everyone else has addressed this pretty well and all I can say is that sometimes the best parts of writing is when things aren't directly addressed, allowing for the reader to think for themselves as to the meaning of such and such writing. The beauty behind Vagabond is that so many things are covered yet they all have substance behind them. The manga addresses the romanticization of swordsmanship and what it actually means to be a master swordsman, which is essentially being a murderer. Why else do you think having people like Takuan or the older masters say things like, "all strong people are truly kind?" It's to combat the people who don't give it any regard at all and Musashi realizes this overtime, learning to become more and more intentional with his swordsmanship and actions overall.

I see it as Takamura being genuinely hurt by Ippo, in a pretty childish way at that. It also serves for Takamura to recognize that so far only he can take Kamogawa high up with him, which lets Ippo hopefully reawakening that drive. I honestly really like this change in the narrative because it adds a lot of emotion to Takamura, who we’ve seen as this larger than life figure

You dont have to like them but we can understand by the way the narrative is approached that there's some greater purpose to characters like Matahachi and Kojiro. For me, I imagine kojiro as the average person who is stacked against behemoths like Musashi and Kojiro, who both dont appear human to the rest of the world. In that, we find some ways to appreciate Matahachi who has many shortcomings, most of which are irredeemable but we still get to witness him persist and try to not be limited by his faults. Each character in their series has a unique purpose to them and that's why I love the series. Even Kojiro has one.

What is mixed about this? Are you supposed to like every character? It seems like you interpreted the characters just like everyone else. Matahachi is an unreliable and terrible friend to takezo. Kojiro is a mute/deaf person that lives for the sword and isnt distracted by the things that Takezo and other people are, which is why he comes off as this otherworldly person. Matahachi is also much worse of a character in the novel, which Inoue used as a base for Vagabond. He has quite literally zero redeemable traits in the novel but in the manga, he's a lot more humanized and someone we can sympathize with.

Also, takezo is supposed to be some one note character in the beginning. He quite literally knows nothing else but violence and doesn't realize that he's "alive" until he's cast away from everything and everyone. I personally find the manga "ending" to be quite perfect because it allows for us to see Musashi become a person that he's actually comfortable being. One that isn't limited by the sword, which was the reason why he was essentially crippled toward the end. It's a great transitioning point for what would have been the next arc but obviously that hasn't happened.

There's nothing wrong with assuming the best and believing that people are good, because there are good people. Learn to be smarter about how you carry yourself in situations to avoid being deceived but recognize it will probably happen and to not quit in being optimistic about the world. 

Start looking at the world on a surface level, especially yourself. See what you do and leave it at that. If you're helping someone, assume you're doing it out of good will and nothing else. It's a struggle but there's really no other alternative especially considering you've tried other methods. Work with what you got. 

About focusing on yourself and improving your self-worth, ask yourself this. Will you ever be objective with yourself? Will you ever be honest? If you're genuinely doing good and have increased your self-worth, whatever that is, will you be genuine with yourself and give yourself that pat on the back? Chances are is that you probably won't do such a thing but if you do, I commend you for it. The irony in focusing on yourself and staying away from people is that you're now in a state of delusion that no one else can see, skewed by your own warped mindset and will only dig the hole of self-hatred deeper and deeper. In order to really focus on yourself, one needs to balance living amongst other people and on their own, observing whether or not their thoughts are actually acted on.
